items.title: Can Borussia Dortmund finally end their title wait? Three big questions for Bundesliga leaders
items.summary: Niko Kovac’s team lead the way and, with Bayern Munich wounded, have a golden chance to be German champions for the first time in 15 years Borussia Dortmund’s dreams have a habit of becoming nightmares, like when they somehow handed Bayern Munich the Bundesliga title on the final day of the 2022-23 season. Or when an 89th-minute Arjen Robben goal won the 2013 Champions League final for the same opponents. Whenever Dortmund suffer heartbreak, it usually involves Bayern.

items.title: Fifa staff asked to attend interviews as Infantino sell-off scheme investigated
items.summary: Democrats to examine Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal Infantino could be subpoenaed to give evidence A number of past and present Fifa employees have received letters requesting they attend interviews for a congressional investigation into the global governing body sparked by the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal. Letters were sent on Wednesday to a number of staff along with a handful of former employees who held senior positions. They have been asked by Democrats on the House judiciary committee to give evidence as efforts gather pace to examine Gianni Infantino’s failed FFE scheme along with links between Fifa and the Trump administration.

I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity.

items.title: Pochettino claims officials ‘punished’ Manchester United in chaotic Sporting draw
items.summary: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes.

items.title: Oliver Glasner criticises Nottingham Forest players for not learning English
items.summary: ‘Players are here for four years and can’t speak English’ Glasner has held talks with owner over January moves Nottingham Forest’s manager, Oliver Glasner, believes standards at the club were not good enough before his arrival as he questioned why some of his squad cannot speak English after a number of years in the country. Glasner was tempted to move to the City Ground by the owner, Evangelos Marinakis, after winning the FA Cup and Conference League at Crystal Palace. However, Forest have won two of their opening 11 Premier League games and sit outside the relegation zone only on goal difference.

items.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
items.summary: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford.

items.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
items.summary: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe.

items.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
items.summary: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was.
